knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Falling dust from high points lands on surfaces that are dusted later, so high work comes first.
Planning one tool per pass removes the repeated passes. Skipping areas or rushing does not fix the sequence.
The extension duster reaches high corners and fittings from the floor.

practicalCriteria: Dusts high points first and then the desk-level surfaces, without dusting any surface twice.
Walks the room in one direction and returns each item to its original place.
Uses an extension duster for high work and does not stand on furniture.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% pass mark, which for three questions means all three correct. Practical sign-off is separate and observed by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of one dusting route
Dusting route noted on the job sheet
stopWorkCriteria: Worker stands on furniture to reach a high point
Items broken or left displaced after dusting
